spine: Keep content, authority and history together while separating what cryptography verifies from what still requires judgment.
art: A reconstructable information parcel: protected bricks reassemble the object, a history ribbon travels with it, and different keys expose reading and verification capabilities separately.
lines: OpenDSU asks what must travel with data for it to remain controllable and verifiable.
The book explains a conceptual framework, rather than documenting one frozen software release.
Its central relationships connect protected content, authority, reconstructable structure, and verifiable history.
A cryptographic commitment can establish integrity without proving the truth of the content.
Readers gain distinctions for evaluating digital trust without asking one mechanism to guarantee everything.
